title: Claude Certified Architect – Foundations: Mixed-format Practice Exams
question_format: Single-answer and multiple-response questions; select exactly the stated number of answers.
note: Original practice questions based on the published curriculum and documentation; not official exam items.

questions.question: A team wants shared conventions and private developer preferences in Claude Code. Which placements fit? (Select TWO answers.)

options.text: Store enforced access policy only as prose
Commit personal API tokens into CLAUDE.md
Require every developer to paste all conventions per turn
Put personal cross-project guidance in ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md
Put shared project guidance in version-controlled CLAUDE.md

questions.explanation: Project instructions are shared; user instructions are personal. Permissions need executable policy.

questions.question: A refund agent must verify identity before issuing money. Which controls enforce this requirement? (Select TWO answers.)

options.text: Treat a subagent summary as proof of authorization
Assume tool order follows the wording of the prompt
Check verification state in the refund handler
Use a PreToolUse gate to deny refunds without verified state
Use PostToolUse to prevent an already completed transfer

questions.explanation: Validate before the side effect and enforce the prerequisite in executable controls.

questions.question: A long customer session is compacted. What should survive in a separate case record? (Select TWO answers.)

options.text: Exact transaction identifiers and amounts
Only a statement that the customer has a problem
Every repeated greeting
All unrelated raw search results
Current issue status and unresolved commitments

questions.explanation: Preserve action-critical facts independently of a lossy narrative summary.

questions.question: An extractor returns valid JSON but assigns values to the wrong invoice. What should validation include? (Select TWO answers.)

options.text: Business rules beyond schema shape
Checks that identifiers and values match source evidence
Only a JSON parser
Drop all source identifiers to simplify output
Assume strict JSON guarantees factual correctness

questions.explanation: Schema compliance validates shape; factual alignment and business rules require additional checks.

questions.question: A CI code reviewer must produce machine-readable findings reliably. Which practices help? (Select TWO answers.)

options.text: Handle run failures and validate the returned findings
Give the reviewer unrestricted deployment credentials
Run an interactive approval dialog in an unattended job
Use non-interactive execution with an explicit output contract
Treat process success as proof that every finding is correct

questions.explanation: Automation needs explicit outputs plus failure handling and content validation.

questions.question: A lead agent delegates vendor research to isolated subagents. What should each assignment provide? (Select TWO answers.)

options.text: Relevant constraints and source requirements
An assumption that other subagents share their findings automatically
A bounded objective and expected output format
Permission to spawn unlimited workers
The complete unrelated conversation history

questions.explanation: Explicit objectives, boundaries, and output contracts prevent gaps and duplication.

questions.question: A classification prompt confuses two neighboring categories. Which example improvements are appropriate? (Select TWO answers.)

options.text: Include contrasting borderline cases
Use inconsistent labels to encourage flexibility
Include examples that contradict the rules without explanation
Add only more examples of the easiest class
Show the intended output format consistently

questions.explanation: Representative edge cases and consistent outputs teach the intended decision boundary.

questions.question: A document pipeline always extracts fields, checks them, then writes a summary. Which design provides the clearest control flow? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Concurrent voting on every sentence.
Prompt chaining through the known stages.
An unrestricted agent with all tools.
Dynamic task planning at each document.

questions.explanation: Known sequential stages fit prompt chaining.

questions.question: A customer asks to replace a damaged item, change a delivery address, and check warranty coverage. What should the coordinator do? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Escalate immediately because the request has three parts.
Answer only the first request and wait.
Decompose the concerns, investigate relevant parts, and give a unified response.
Start three unrelated conversations without account context.

questions.explanation: A compound request requires coverage of each concern and one coherent resolution.

questions.question: A support system classifies requests as billing, account access, or technical issues and sends each to a specialized process. Which pattern is this? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Evaluator-optimizer.
Prompt chaining.
Routing.
Voting.

questions.explanation: Routing selects a specialized downstream process based on the input category.

questions.question: A source contract contains no renewal date, yet the extraction schema requires one. Which design avoids pressuring Claude to invent a date? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Repeat the extraction until a date appears.
Ask Claude to estimate a likely date.
Use a higher temperature.
Make the field nullable or optional and return null when absent.

questions.explanation: An absent source value cannot be recovered by retrying; the schema should allow missing information to be represented honestly.

questions.question: An MCP inventory call times out after its handler starts. Which response design helps recovery? (Select TWO answers.)

options.text: Return an empty successful inventory list
Set isError to true in the tool result
Include actionable details about the transient failure
Describe errorCategory as a mandatory MCP field
Retry without a bound until success

questions.explanation: MCP defines isError; useful recovery metadata can be application-defined.

questions.question: A research branch fails after returning useful findings. What should the coordinator preserve? (Select TWO answers.)

options.text: A claim that every source was checked
No record of attempted recovery
A successful empty result for the failed part
An explicit description of the remaining coverage gap
Usable partial findings with provenance

questions.explanation: Partial evidence and visible gaps allow transparent synthesis and targeted recovery.

questions.question: A document summarizer follows detailed format instructions but alternates between prose and tables across runs. What is the best first prompt change? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Add a few representative input-output examples in the desired format.
Ask for a confidence score before each paragraph.
Append the format instruction ten times.
Raise the temperature.

questions.explanation: Relevant examples demonstrate the exact target format and improve consistency more directly than repeated prose instructions.

questions.question: A review agent gives detailed feedback on early files but shallow feedback on later files. What is the best structural fix? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Stop after the first five files.
Repeat the instruction to be thorough several times.
Increase the maximum number of files in one prompt.
Review each file in a focused pass, then run a cross-file integration pass.

questions.explanation: Focused local passes reduce attention dilution; an integration pass catches cross-file issues.

questions.question: An agent needs customer profile lookup and shipment tracking. How can descriptions distinguish the tools? (Select TWO answers.)

options.text: State when to use each tool instead of the other
Give both the description Look up information
Depend only on short tool names
Hide returned fields from the model
State the identifiers each accepts

questions.explanation: Input contracts and explicit use boundaries resolve overlapping descriptions.

questions.question: A claims assistant summarizes each completed turn. Later it forgets an exact deductible and policy number. Which design most directly protects those facts? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Ask the model to reconstruct the missing numbers
Remove all earlier turns after summarization
Keep a structured case-facts record and carry it into later requests
Increase the model temperature

questions.explanation: Critical identifiers and amounts should be stored separately from lossy narrative summaries and supplied when needed.

questions.question: A synthesis subagent is asked to write a market brief, but the parent never includes the research subagent's findings in its prompt. What is the most likely failure? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: The research agent's tools become available to the synthesis agent.
The synthesis agent can recover the findings from shared memory.
The Agent SDK automatically replays every parent tool result to it.
The synthesis agent lacks those findings because its context is separate.

questions.explanation: A subagent starts with isolated context and needs relevant prior findings passed explicitly.

questions.question: An agent is investigating why an unfamiliar service intermittently fails, and each clue may change the next diagnostic step. Which approach fits? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: A fixed sequence that never changes.
A single response without tools.
Adaptive decomposition that revises the plan as evidence arrives.
A routing classifier only.

questions.explanation: Unknown root causes require a plan that can respond to new findings.

questions.question: A team wants Claude to label code-review findings as critical, major, or minor consistently. What should the prompt include? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Only dictionary definitions of the three words.
Representative code examples with the expected severity and a brief rationale.
A command to choose critical whenever uncertain.
The team's preferred temperature setting.

questions.explanation: Concrete labeled examples anchor each severity level and clarify the intended boundary between categories.

questions.question: A nightly batch returns results in an order different from submission order. How should the application match each result to its source record? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Compare the text length.
Use each request's unique custom_id.
Rely on the array position.
Sort by token usage.

questions.explanation: custom_id is the caller-supplied correlation key for matching individual batch results to requests.

questions.question: A prior session analyzed configuration files that were substantially rewritten overnight. The agent now cites removed settings. What is the best recovery? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Fork the stale history.
Resume again without mentioning the changes.
Ask the model to ignore all tool results while retaining them.
Start fresh with a structured summary and re-read changed files.

questions.explanation: A fresh session avoids stale tool results while a curated summary preserves still-valid findings.

questions.question: A single review of a 20-file pull request is deep on the first files and shallow on the rest. What workflow best addresses this? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Review only the first five files.
Review each file in a focused pass, then perform a separate cross-file integration pass.
Replace review with a confidence score from one pass.
Increase the context window only.

questions.explanation: Focused local passes give each file attention; an integration pass then checks interactions and inconsistencies across files.

questions.question: In a Claude Code session where Grep and Glob are available, a developer needs all files named *.test.tsx. Which tool matches file paths by pattern? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Grep
Glob
Read
Bash only

questions.explanation: Glob locates files by path or filename pattern.

questions.question: A request supplies an extraction tool with the default tool_choice of auto. What behavior must the caller allow for? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Claude always calls the extraction tool.
The API rejects all text responses.
Claude calls every available tool in order.
Claude may respond in text without calling a tool.

questions.explanation: With auto, Claude decides whether a tool call is needed, so a text-only response remains possible.

questions.question: One Messages API response contains two tool_use blocks with different IDs. How should the application continue? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Treat the presence of two blocks as end_turn.
Run both calls and return a tool_result matched to each tool_use ID.
Execute only the first block and discard the second.
Merge both calls into one new tool ID.

questions.explanation: Each client-tool request needs its own result paired by tool_use_id.

questions.question: A payment agent must verify account ownership before sending funds. Which control best guarantees the order? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: A programmatic gate that rejects send_funds until verification succeeds.
Several examples of correct behavior.
A post-payment audit only.
A reminder in the user prompt.

questions.explanation: A prerequisite gate blocks the sensitive tool before execution if verification has not succeeded.

questions.question: A CI script uses --output-format json and --json-schema. Where should it read the schema-conforming result? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: The top-level usage field
The stderr stream only
The first line of the text result
The structured_output field in the JSON envelope

questions.explanation: The JSON envelope contains metadata; the validated final value appears under structured_output.

questions.question: An invoice extractor succeeds on tables but misses amounts written in narrative paragraphs. Which examples should be added? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Only more clean tables.
Narrative and mixed-format invoices showing the correct extracted fields.
Examples with empty output for every narrative invoice.
Examples of unrelated document types.

questions.explanation: Few-shot examples should target the failing document structure, including how the value is extracted from narrative text.

questions.question: A server exposes a database schema as an MCP resource. Who determines how that resource enters model context? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: The host application or client
The resource URI itself
Every tool call automatically
The schema's row count

questions.explanation: MCP resources are application-driven; the host decides how to present or attach them.

questions.question: A refund tool rejects a technically valid request because it exceeds a policy limit. What should the agent do? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Retry the same request immediately
Silently mark the refund complete
Follow the stated escalation or alternate workflow
Treat it as a network timeout

questions.explanation: A business-rule failure is not repaired by resending identical arguments; recovery needs another authorized path.

questions.question: After a long repository investigation, an assistant forgets the specific dependency path it found earlier. Which practice best preserves it? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Read every file again at each turn
Rely on a larger context window alone
Replace the dependency path with a generic design pattern
Save precise findings and file paths in a durable scratchpad

questions.explanation: A scratchpad externalizes precise findings so they can be retrieved after context fills with other outputs.

questions.question: A synthesis agent paraphrases subagent findings and loses their citations. What should subagents provide? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Structured findings with claim-to-source mappings that the synthesizer must preserve
Confidence labels with no URLs
Only source titles, without claims
A single unstructured narrative

questions.explanation: Explicit provenance must travel with each claim through synthesis and appear in the final answer.

questions.question: An extracted invoice has valid JSON, but its line items total 430 while the stated total is 480; the original document is available. What is the best next step? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Retry with only the phrase try again.
Accept it because the JSON schema passed.
Retry with the original invoice, the failed extraction, and the specific discrepancy.
Delete the stated total field.

questions.explanation: A semantic validator should detect the mismatch and give Claude precise feedback plus the source and prior output for correction.

questions.question: Claude generates a function and is then asked in the same conversation to review it. Subtle bugs keep passing review. What is the strongest architectural change? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Raise the output token limit for generation.
Ask the same conversation to review more carefully.
Use a fresh review invocation that sees the code but not the generation history.
Remove all tests before review.

questions.explanation: An independent reviewer lacks the generating conversation's prior decisions and can assess the artifact afresh.

questions.question: In a Claude Code session where Grep and Glob are available, a developer needs to find every file that calls processOrder. Which tool searches file contents? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Write
Grep
Glob
Edit

questions.explanation: Grep searches text inside files; a caller name is content, not a path pattern.

questions.question: Unit tests are co-located with source files across dozens of folders. The same test conventions should load only when a test file is used. What is the best configuration? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Put every test rule in root CLAUDE.md
Copy CLAUDE.md into every folder
Use .claude/rules/ with a paths glob for test files
Create a skill developers must invoke manually

questions.explanation: A path-scoped rule applies to matching files across directories without loading irrelevant conventions for other files.

questions.question: Claude Code keeps applying a known API migration inconsistently despite a prose description. What should the developer provide next? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Several exact before-and-after examples
A higher turn limit
A longer abstract description
Only the file tree

questions.explanation: Concrete input/output examples communicate the intended transformation more precisely than repeated prose.

questions.question: A codebase-analysis skill produces extensive file listings that should not fill the main conversation. Which frontmatter setting addresses this? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: model: inherit
argument-hint: files
context: fork
paths: all

questions.explanation: context: fork runs the skill in an isolated subagent context and returns its result to the parent.

questions.question: A tool requires an order_id but sometimes receives no identifier. Which part of its definition should mark that field mandatory? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: The input schema's required array
The tool result's content
The server transport
A resource URI

questions.explanation: A JSON Schema required list identifies mandatory input properties.

questions.question: A multi-agent support system has separate billing and shipping roles. How should tools be allocated? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Give every specialist every available tool
Split tools across servers but expose all to every agent
Give each specialist only tools relevant to its role
Give no tools to specialists

questions.explanation: Role-scoped tool sets reduce irrelevant choices and limit unintended capabilities.

questions.question: A stock lookup reaches the tool handler but its upstream API times out. Which response best supports model recovery? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: A tool result with isError: true and actionable retry guidance
A normal success result saying Operation failed
An empty resource list
A different tool name

questions.explanation: An execution failure belongs in a tool result marked isError so the model can see the cause and decide whether to retry.

questions.question: A team must block a dangerous shell command in every Claude Code session. Which mechanism provides an enforced control? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: A permission deny rule in settings
An example in a skill description
A warning in CLAUDE.md
A reminder in the first prompt

questions.explanation: CLAUDE.md guides model behavior but is not an enforcement layer. A deny rule is evaluated by the client.

questions.question: A team wants to compare two migration strategies from the same completed analysis while preserving the original investigation. Which session action fits? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Start two blank sessions with no baseline.
Continue the original twice without branching.
Fork the session into independent branches.
Clear the session transcript.

questions.explanation: Forking gives each alternative the shared starting context and a separate continuation.

questions.question: A long research packet has critical findings buried among many source excerpts. The synthesizer repeatedly misses them. What should change first? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Repeat a generic instruction to read carefully
Put a concise key-findings summary first, then labeled detail sections
Delete all citations to shorten the packet
Increase the number of subagents

questions.explanation: Position and structure affect retrieval from long context; front-load key findings and keep detailed evidence organized.

questions.question: A travel assistant receives stop_reason "tool_use" with a client-tool request to check a train schedule. What should the application do next? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Ask Claude to repeat the same request without tools.
Start a new unrelated conversation with the tool output.
Return the assistant text as the final answer.
Execute the requested tool, append the assistant response and matching tool_result, then call Claude again.

questions.explanation: A client tool runs in the application; its result must be sent back before Claude can finish the turn.

questions.question: A code-review assistant reports many naming preferences as defects. Which system-prompt change most directly improves precision? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Tell it to be conservative.
Increase max_tokens so it can justify every finding.
Define reportable bug and security categories and explicitly exclude style preferences.
Ask it to report only findings above 90% self-reported confidence.

questions.explanation: Explicit inclusion and exclusion criteria give the model an actionable decision boundary; vague caution and raw confidence do not.

questions.question: Three inventory tools return dates in different formats. Which mechanism can normalize their returned data before Claude reads it? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: A system prompt asking Claude to guess each format.
An iteration cap on the agent loop.
A PreToolUse hook that inspects tool arguments.
A PostToolUse hook that transforms tool output.

questions.explanation: PostToolUse receives the completed result and can standardize what the model sees.

questions.question: Two credible reports give different values for a market indicator and use different measurement periods. How should a synthesis report present them? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Show both values with source, period, and possible methodological differences
Omit the indicator entirely
Average the figures without qualification
Keep only the newer report

questions.explanation: Preserving both attributed values and their temporal context avoids false certainty.

questions.question: A research subagent times out after collecting two of three requested documents. What should it return to its coordinator? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: The two findings plus the failure type, attempted query, and missing coverage
A fatal error with no documents
A fabricated summary of the third document
An empty successful result

questions.explanation: Structured partial failure preserves useful evidence and gives the coordinator a basis for retry or disclosure.

questions.question: A document-reading subagent only needs approved document URLs. Which interface best follows least privilege? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: A tool that also changes permissions
A general shell command executor
An unrestricted fetch_url tool
A constrained load_document tool that validates URLs

questions.explanation: A constrained tool exposes the needed capability without broad arbitrary URL access.

questions.question: A developer paused an Agent SDK task yesterday; the repository has not changed. They need to continue the same investigation with its prior tool results. What should they use? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Discard the prior history and rerun everything.
Resume the specific prior session.
Fork into two independent branches.
A completely fresh session.

questions.explanation: Resume restores the prior conversation when that context remains valid.

questions.question: A payment integration has three viable architectures and affects several services. How should Claude Code begin? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Directly edit the first service
Run /compact before reading code
Create a global skill for the integration
Enter plan mode and compare approaches before edits

questions.explanation: Plan mode is suited to ambiguous, multi-file architectural work that needs exploration before implementation.

questions.question: Two developers need the same MCP server configuration when they clone a project. Where should it be stored? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: In the model's auto memory
Only in one developer's ~/.claude.json
.mcp.json at the project root, committed to version control
In a private chat message

questions.explanation: Claude Code project-scoped MCP servers are configured in the repository's .mcp.json.

questions.question: A team knows every step of invoice extraction in advance and needs predictable execution. Which architecture fits best? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: An open-ended agent that invents steps on every invoice.
A tool-use loop with no stopping condition.
A group of agents that always debate every field.
A predefined workflow with fixed steps.

questions.explanation: A workflow is appropriate when the code path is known and consistency matters.

questions.question: A new engineer clones a repository but Claude Code does not follow the team's naming standard. The standard exists only in the lead engineer's home directory. Where should it go? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: The repository's CLAUDE.md or .claude/CLAUDE.md
A global MCP server configuration
The new engineer's ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md only
A prompt pasted into every session

questions.explanation: Project instructions are version-controlled and shared with the team; user instructions in a home directory are personal.

questions.question: A data conversion must preserve nulls, handle empty arrays, and satisfy a schema. What gives Claude Code the clearest iterative feedback? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: A personal preference in settings
Failing tests covering the specified cases
A command to compact context
An open-ended request to improve quality

questions.explanation: Tests make expected behavior and edge cases observable through pass/fail results.

questions.question: A stack trace identifies a one-line condition that must change in one function. The fix and location are known. Which workflow is most efficient? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Use direct execution, then run the relevant check
Start with a broad architecture plan
Fork a research skill
Rewrite the entire module

questions.explanation: A clear, limited edit does not need a separate planning phase, but it should still be verified.

questions.question: A support tool returns forty fields, but the task needs only order ID, status, and amount. What should the application do before the next model turn? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Trim the tool result to relevant fields while retaining necessary identifiers
Pass all fields in case they become useful
Repeat the same tool call
Convert the result to a longer prose paragraph

questions.explanation: Filtering irrelevant tool output reduces context use while retaining facts required for the task.

questions.question: A repository needs a reusable /release-check workflow with supporting checklists. Which path fits the Skills system? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: .claude/skills/release-check.md
.claude/rules/release-check.json
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md
.claude/skills/release-check/SKILL.md

questions.explanation: A project skill is a directory containing SKILL.md; supporting files can sit alongside it.

questions.question: A client-tool response contains two independent tool_use blocks. Which application actions are required? (Select TWO answers.)

options.text: Put tool results into the system prompt
Return only the first result and omit the second ID
Assume a text block means the tool loop is complete
Process both calls under application policy, executing allowed actions or returning explicit failure results
Match each tool_result to its tool_use_id

questions.explanation: Each client call needs a corresponding result; the assistant content and IDs must be preserved.

questions.question: A workflow has known extraction, validation, and publication stages. Which design choices fit deterministic stage requirements? (Select TWO answers.)

options.text: Let a prompt alone guarantee the publication gate
Add independent agents for every line of output
Require successful validation before enabling publication
Permit publication whenever the model sounds confident
Represent stage transitions in application control flow

questions.explanation: Known prerequisites are best encoded as explicit workflow gates.

questions.question: A summarizer merges two credible but conflicting estimates. Which metadata should remain visible? (Select TWO answers.)

options.text: Only their unsourced arithmetic mean
Measurement periods and definitions
A fabricated consensus figure
Only whichever value appears first
The source associated with each value

questions.explanation: Attribution and measurement context let readers assess the disagreement.

questions.question: A structured-output request returns HTTP 200. Which conditions still require special handling before parsing as a complete business record? (Select TWO answers.)

options.text: stop_reason is refusal
The response contains ordinary whitespace
The schema has descriptive field names
The request includes a system prompt
stop_reason is max_tokens

questions.explanation: Refusals and token-limited output can violate the expected complete structured response.

questions.question: An MCP query returns no rows after successful execution. Which interpretations are correct? (Select TWO answers.)

options.text: It must always set isError to true
The result should distinguish no matches from failed access
It proves the database was unreachable
This can be a valid empty result
It requires unlimited identical retries

questions.explanation: A completed query with no matches differs from a query that could not run.

questions.question: Claude returns a text block saying it will check a record and also returns a tool_use block. What should control the loop? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: The response stop_reason, which indicates a tool call is pending.
Whether the sentence contains the word "check".
The first content block being text.
A fixed two-iteration limit.

questions.explanation: Text can accompany a tool call; stop_reason identifies why the response stopped.

questions.question: A prompt embeds task rules and third-party documents. Which changes improve separation of instructions from evidence? (Select TWO answers.)

options.text: Use descriptive delimiters or XML tags around source content
Promote document instructions into the system prompt
Treat every imperative in a document as user intent
Explicitly define source content as data to analyze
Remove the actual user task from the prompt

questions.explanation: Clear boundaries help Claude interpret documents as evidence; they do not turn data into authority.

questions.question: A shared .mcp.json connects to a remote service. Which practices support safe team use? (Select TWO answers.)

options.text: Use environment-variable references for credentials
Review and approve project-scoped servers before interactive use
Store a teammate token as a literal for convenience
Assume a private repository is a secret store
Trust server descriptions as authorization grants

questions.explanation: Shared configuration should not contain secrets, and project servers have an approval boundary.

questions.question: A drafting agent creates a proposal; a second agent checks it against an explicit rubric and returns targeted feedback for revision. Which pattern is this? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Routing.
Tool search.
Evaluator-optimizer.
Prompt caching.

questions.explanation: The evaluator checks an output against criteria and feeds a revision loop.

questions.question: A style guide prefers title case headings, and an occasional inconsistency has little consequence. Which control is proportionate? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Block every response with a pre-execution hook.
Require human approval for every heading.
Prompt guidance describing the preferred style.
Disable all model-generated headings.

questions.explanation: Low-stakes preferences can be expressed through prompts; deterministic gates are for requirements that must never be skipped.

questions.question: A team proposes Message Batches solely to reduce cost for an interactive checkout assistant. What is the central objection? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Batch cannot use vision inputs.
Batch has asynchronous completion and no immediate-response latency guarantee.
Batch results are always in submission order.
Batch does not accept system messages.

questions.explanation: The cost discount is useful only when the workflow can tolerate delayed completion.

questions.question: An agent has many near-identical transformation tools that all accept data and an operation. What can reduce selection complexity without removing capability? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: A parameterized transform tool with an operation enum
A separate MCP server for each transform while exposing all
Longer names for all transforms only
Giving every transform to every subagent

questions.explanation: Related operations with a common shape can be consolidated under one well-defined parameterized interface.

questions.question: SQL conventions apply only under migrations/. Which rule design is appropriate? (Select TWO answers.)

options.text: Use MCP installation scope to match source paths
Use a path-scoped file under .claude/rules/
Put access tokens into the rule text
Use paths frontmatter to express the matching files
Load every SQL instruction globally for every task

questions.explanation: Path-specific rules condition convention loading on relevant files.

questions.question: A single analyze_document tool extracts fields, summarizes text, and verifies claims, and Claude often chooses the wrong behavior. What interface change is most direct? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Split it into purpose-specific tools with clear contracts
Move the tool to another MCP server without changing it
Hide all output schemas
Use the same description for all operations

questions.explanation: Distinct jobs are easier to select when each has a clear name and input/output contract.

questions.question: In an orchestrator-workers design, who should decide which workers to invoke and combine their outputs? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Every worker independently, without coordination.
The first worker that finishes.
The end user after each tool call.
The orchestrator.

questions.explanation: The orchestrator dynamically decomposes the task, delegates work, and synthesizes results.

questions.question: An application must resume a specific older SDK conversation rather than whichever session ran most recently. What should it retain? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: The number of tool calls.
Only the latest answer text.
Only the model name.
The session ID and pass it to resume.

questions.explanation: A specific prior conversation is identified by its session ID.

questions.question: A reusable release skill must run only when a developer invokes it. Which settings or expectations fit? (Select TWO answers.)

options.text: Describe it vaguely so Claude invokes it more often
Set user-invocable: false to make it manual-only
Set disable-model-invocation: true
Keep the skill callable by the user through its slash command
Assume the skill bypasses permission checks

questions.explanation: disable-model-invocation prevents automatic use while keeping user invocation available.

questions.question: A team puts errorCategory and isRetryable in structuredContent of an MCP tool error result. How should those fields be understood? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Transport negotiation headers
A replacement for isError
Application-level conventions, not universal MCP protocol fields
Mandatory JSON-RPC envelope fields

Only the model confidence percentage
