questions.question: An exploration lead has a clean architectural summary from Phase 1. A Phase 2 subagent will inspect one component. What context transfer is most efficient? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Provide the relevant summary, component objective, and pointers to evidence
Require it to repeat Phase 1 completely
Provide no prior findings to keep it independent
Send every raw terminal line from Phase 1

questions.explanation: A concise handoff avoids cold-start duplication while preserving useful prior knowledge.

questions.question: An MCP export tool returns a schema-conforming account ID and file URL. Which checks are still necessary before exposing the file? (Select TWO answers.)

options.text: Whether the URL is within the permitted delivery boundary
Whether the requester is authorized for that account
Whether JSON properties are alphabetically ordered
None because outputSchema guarantees authorization
Whether a newer model would prefer the URL

questions.explanation: Output shape does not replace access control or URL validation.

questions.question: A batch processes thousands of independent documents. Which handling supports selective recovery? (Select TWO answers.)

options.text: Treat batch completion as proof of every item success
Assume result order matches submission order
Track each item with a unique custom_id
Discard successful results when one item fails
Inspect each result type and retry eligible failures only

questions.explanation: Batch completion and per-item success differ; identifiers support targeted processing.

questions.question: A prompt improvement raises overall F1 but lowers recall for the safety-critical minority class. Which report best supports review? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Convert all errors into one confidence score
Remove minority-class labels from the test set
Show only the improved overall F1
Show overall and class-level metrics, including the regression and business cost

questions.explanation: Aggregate improvement can mask a harmful segment regression.

questions.question: A strict tool schema validates an account number format, but the operation transfers money to a different tenant. What architectural conclusion follows? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Enforce tenant ownership and transaction policy in the tool/backend
The field should become unrestricted free text
Strict mode should replace backend authorization
A schema-valid call cannot have a business defect

questions.explanation: Constrained generation controls input shape, not the caller right to act on a resource.

questions.question: A broad literature review exceeds a single useful context. Subagents can investigate independent fields, but total token cost matters. Which architecture best fits? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: A fixed answer template without research
Bounded parallel specialists returning compact evidence to a lead
One worker per sentence with unlimited raw transcripts
Every agent rereads all sources and shares all raw logs

questions.explanation: Parallel context can improve breadth, but bounded scope and compression control its cost.

questions.question: A tool returns a large response containing credentials that the model does not need. The action itself is authorized. Which hook phase fits sanitizing the returned content before model consumption? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: No phase; every raw field must reach the model
SessionEnd, after the whole task is over
PostToolUse, with a transformed tool output
PreToolUse as an undo for completed output

questions.explanation: PostToolUse can transform results; it is distinct from deciding whether an action may execute.

questions.question: A team replaces Claude Code default system guidance with only a short review rubric and notices lost coding behavior. Which change preserves defaults while adding the rubric? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Add more tool servers
Use the documented append-system-prompt mechanism
Store the rubric in an API token variable
Assume a replacement system prompt implicitly includes all defaults

questions.explanation: Appending and replacing system guidance have different behavior.

questions.question: A report agent has 25 transformations and occasional customer queries. Which redesigns reduce choice complexity without expanding privilege? (Select TWO answers.)

options.text: Hide required parameter meaning to save tokens
Add administrator tools so errors are easier to fix
Expose only a scoped customer lookup for the occasional query
Merge everything into unrestricted SQL execution
Consolidate compatible transformations with a validated operation selector

questions.explanation: Consolidation reduces redundant choices; constrained cross-role access preserves least privilege.

questions.question: A developer plans a cross-service change and must compare two migration strategies before editing. Which initial workflow fits? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Implement the smaller migration first, then compare architectural options afterward
Use a global convention file as a substitute for the task-specific migration plan
Plan Mode with targeted exploration and a proposed verification plan
Ask a reviewer to approve an approach without inspecting dependency evidence

questions.explanation: Planning fits uncertain, consequential architecture choices before implementation.

questions.question: A project rule says all migrations use UTC, but a nested rule says local time without explaining an exception. Claude alternates behavior. What is the best repair? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Increase the context window
Remove migration tests
Add both rules twice to increase emphasis
Resolve the conflict and express any real exception with a clear scope

questions.explanation: Conflicting instructions require clarification and scoping, not more repetition.

questions.question: A case has two refunds and one replacement. Compaction merges them into a single generic issue. Which state changes protect later actions? (Select TWO answers.)

options.text: Infer which refund the user means from the largest amount
Keep only the latest customer sentiment
Discard completed action status after compaction
Refresh the verified case-facts block independently of narrative summaries
Keep separate issue records with identifiers, amounts, and status

questions.explanation: Structured per-issue state prevents cross-contamination and repeated actions.

questions.question: A new PR review repeats a finding that was acknowledged and intentionally deferred on the previous revision. What context most directly prevents repetition? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: The current diff plus prior finding disposition and any changed assumptions
An instruction to find a fixed number of new defects
A higher temperature
Only the entire repository with no review history

questions.explanation: Iterative review needs prior decisions to distinguish unresolved regressions from deliberate deferrals.

questions.question: A database server lists a schema resource, but the model never receives it. Tool calls repeatedly rediscover table structure. Where should the integration be inspected first? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Whether every table has its own agent
Whether the resource URI is a tool-use ID
Only the sampling temperature
How the host exposes or attaches the resource to model context

questions.explanation: Resource availability on the server does not imply automatic inclusion in model context.

questions.question: An unattended CI reviewer must not edit or deploy. Which controls support that requirement? (Select TWO answers.)

options.text: Explicit handling when a required operation is denied
A prompt saying be careful as the only protection
Production deployment tokens in shared instructions
Automatic permission bypass for every failed action
Tool permissions and backend credentials restricted to the review role

questions.explanation: Use actual access restrictions and a predictable denial path for unattended work.

questions.question: A CI job consumes JSON output from Claude Code. Which safeguards help avoid accepting a failed run as a review result? (Select TWO answers.)

options.text: Treat exit code zero as proof there are no bugs
Check only that stdout is nonempty
Parse stderr as the only source of task results
Inspect run status and the documented output envelope
Validate the findings against the required schema and business meaning

questions.explanation: Transport or run success and valid task findings are separate checks.

questions.question: Claude returns parallel client calls to two sources; one succeeds and one fails. Which next-turn handling is correct? (Select THREE answers.)

options.text: Return a result for each tool_use_id, including the failure
Preserve the original assistant content containing both calls
Move successful source text into the system prompt
Describe tool failure with is_error in the API tool_result
Omit the failed call so Claude can infer its status

questions.explanation: Preserve the call/result contract, and expose the failed client call as an error result.

questions.question: An organization requires a centrally enforced restriction despite developer settings. Where should enforceable policy be configured? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Only a personal CLAUDE.md suggestion
Organization-managed settings and corresponding access controls
Only a comment in a source file
An untrusted document retrieved during the task

questions.explanation: Managed configuration is the documented policy mechanism; prose is not an enforcement boundary.

questions.question: A draft satisfies the acceptance rubric, but an optimizer continues cosmetic rewrites until budget exhaustion. Which transition should the controller enforce? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Every evaluation leads to another rewrite
Discard acceptance criteria after the first pass
Accepted evaluation leads to completion
No draft can complete before the budget is exhausted

questions.explanation: An evaluator-optimizer loop needs a genuine success exit as well as a budget exit.

questions.question: A team enables prompt caching and then doubles the reference corpus, expecting cached input to bypass context limits. What is the correct assessment? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Cached tokens still count; curate or compact context separately
Caching turns context tokens into permanent external memory
A cache hit guarantees no context degradation
The output budget becomes unlimited on a cache hit

questions.explanation: Caching changes processing economics, not the model context capacity.

questions.question: A support classifier examples are all short, polite, and from one region, while production includes long multilingual complaints. Which change addresses the coverage problem? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Sort examples only by length
Repeat the same easy example more often
Use diverse, representative examples and evaluate the missing segments
Assume the model will infer every missing decision boundary

questions.explanation: Examples should reflect meaningful production variation, with evaluation confirming generalization.

questions.question: A long input contains many repeated tool responses and one decisive fact. The model misses the fact despite unused token capacity. What is the best first intervention? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Increase max_tokens only
Remove redundant output and foreground the decisive evidence with clear structure
Repeat all irrelevant results again
Treat unused context capacity as proof the prompt is optimal

questions.explanation: Useful context curation matters even before the token limit is reached.

questions.question: A deployment skill should be discoverable to users but never auto-invoked by Claude. Which choices are correct? (Select TWO answers.)

options.text: Retain deliberate user invocation through /skill-name
Assume allowed-tools grants all backend rights
Set user-invocable: false as the only control
Set disable-model-invocation: true
Use an irrelevant description to hide side effects

questions.explanation: Manual invocation control is distinct from user visibility and from authorization.

questions.question: A repository proposes a new third-party MCP server with a shared endpoint and personal tokens. Which onboarding actions are appropriate? (Select TWO answers.)

options.text: Use environment-variable references for personal secrets
Commit a working personal token to prove the configuration
Assume resource descriptions grant backend permissions
Treat project configuration as automatically trusted by every clone
Review server capabilities and trust before approval

questions.explanation: Shared configuration requires trust review and secret separation.

questions.question: An extraction model gives 0.99 confidence on a new supplier layout but frequently swaps subtotal and total. What should determine automation for that layout? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Measured field-level performance on labeled examples of that layout
Validate schema shape only and infer that field assignment is correct
Keep automatic acceptance because the model confidence exceeds the old global threshold
Use the aggregate accuracy of all previous supplier formats as the only evidence

questions.explanation: Observed correctness in the relevant segment is stronger evidence than uncalibrated confidence.

questions.question: Two research sources report different revenue figures with different fiscal periods. Which synthesis practices preserve evidence? (Select TWO answers.)

options.text: Describe the unresolved comparability issue
Select the larger figure to avoid understatement
Erase dates to simplify the table
Average the figures and call the result published revenue
Keep each figure linked to its source and reporting period

questions.explanation: Conflicts require attribution and methodological context, not invented consensus.

questions.question: An agent must look up a customer ID, then use that returned ID to request eligibility. The team wants lower latency. Which optimization preserves dependencies? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Run both calls simultaneously with a guessed ID
Use tool_choice any to eliminate the dependency
Parallelize independent work while keeping eligibility after the lookup
Omit the lookup and let the model invent an ID

questions.explanation: Only independent operations are safe to parallelize; dependent arguments must come from the earlier result.

questions.question: A third-party MCP tool declares readOnlyHint. The host uses that annotation as proof that authorization checks can be skipped. What is wrong? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Read-only data can never be sensitive
Annotations are hints and do not establish trust or authorization
MCP requires all tools to be writable
The annotation changes the user identity

questions.explanation: Tool annotations should not replace security checks, especially for untrusted servers.

questions.question: An approval can be revoked between planning and tool execution. Which controls protect a destructive action? (Select TWO answers.)

options.text: Use PostToolUse to prevent a completed deletion
Deny the action before execution if current approval is absent
Recheck authoritative authorization at execution time
Treat a schema-valid request as current approval
Rely on the approval copied into an old summary

questions.explanation: Approval is live application state; enforce it before the side effect rather than trusting stale conversation data.

questions.question: An evaluator checks generated figures without seeing the original table. It flags plausible formatting issues but misses wrong totals. Which input is most needed? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Only the generator explanation
The original evidence and an arithmetic accuracy criterion
An instruction to trust schema-valid numbers
A larger list of stylistic adjectives

questions.explanation: Reviewers need independent evidence and task-specific criteria to detect factual errors.

questions.question: After a tool is renamed for clarity, routing still follows an old system instruction naming the previous behavior. What is the most direct investigation? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Check the joint instructions and tool descriptions for conflicting routing rules
Increase output length
Remove parameter validation
Add a second server with the same tool

questions.explanation: Selection is affected by both tool descriptions and surrounding instructions.

questions.question: A review rubric says identify defects but does not define whether naming preferences count. Reviewers disagree widely. What should be changed first? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Require the reviewer to produce a fixed number of findings per file
Define defect categories, severity, and concrete inclusion criteria
Raise the severity of every naming comment so reviewers agree on priority
Add independent reviewers while leaving the defect definition unchanged

questions.explanation: Explicit criteria address ambiguous judgment boundaries before adding more reviewers.

questions.question: A payment worker loses its connection after submitting a charge. The coordinator cannot tell whether the charge committed. Which recovery controls are appropriate? (Select TWO answers.)

options.text: Assume the session transcript rolls back the charge
Retry every timed-out charge with a fresh transaction identity
Mark the charge as failed solely from the network timeout
Query transaction state before deciding to submit again
Use an application-supported idempotency mechanism for repeat submissions

questions.explanation: A timeout leaves execution uncertain; inspect durable state and make repeats safe in the payment system.

questions.question: A developer keeps adding instructions to CLAUDE.md whenever Claude makes a mistake. The file now contains stale exceptions and repeated rules. Which next step is most useful? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Audit and simplify the file, keeping specific testable guidance
Stop verifying results because instructions are long
Move secrets into the file so it has more context
Append another generic reminder to obey everything

questions.explanation: Instruction maintenance should remove noise and contradictions rather than accumulate reminders indefinitely.

questions.question: A deterministic form task already meets accuracy and latency targets with one model call. A proposal adds a planner and three reviewers without a measured failure. What is the best next decision? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Replace the baseline before establishing an evaluation set for the new design
Adopt the expanded design because independent review always pays for its latency
Tune the expanded design only on the examples that motivated the proposal
Keep the simpler baseline and evaluate additions against a concrete unmet criterion

questions.explanation: Additional orchestration needs evidence that its quality gain justifies latency, cost, and complexity.

questions.question: A batch item requires a client-tool lookup and a subsequent model turn using that lookup. Why does a single submitted request not finish the full workflow automatically? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: The application must execute the client call and submit the follow-up request
The tool definition itself executes the backend
Batch processing forbids every kind of tool use
The batch service automatically gains database credentials

questions.explanation: Batching model requests does not implement the application client-tool loop.

questions.question: A resumed coding session moves to a new host. Which prerequisites must the application consider separately? (Select TWO answers.)

options.text: Automatic rollback of all actions since interruption
Availability and consistency of the working files
Automatic recreation of every external database state
A guarantee that old credentials remain authorized
Availability of the persisted session history

questions.explanation: Session continuation restores conversation history, not every environment or external side effect.

questions.question: An adapter maps MCP failures into Claude API tool results. Which field mappings or distinctions are correct? (Select THREE answers.)

options.text: Both protocols require errorCategory in their standard envelopes
Recovery categories may be defined by the application
MCP tool results use isError
Claude API tool_result blocks use is_error
A valid empty lookup must always become an error

questions.explanation: The error flags differ across the two interfaces; recovery taxonomy is application-level.

questions.question: A personal tool experiment should load in every project for one developer, while a team integration is version-controlled. Which scope pairing fits? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Local scope for cross-project sharing with every teammate
User scope for the experiment; project .mcp.json for the team integration
Project scope for both and commit personal credentials
Put both only in a transient conversation

questions.explanation: MCP user scope is personal across projects; project scope is shared via repository configuration.

questions.question: Two research runs use different valid search paths and reach equally supported answers. An evaluator fails one because its tool sequence differs from a reference trace. What should change? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Evaluate only citation count and ignore whether sources support the claims
Require the reference tool sequence even when another route satisfies all constraints
Use final-answer fluency as a proxy for evidence quality
Grade outcome quality and relevant process constraints rather than one exact trace

questions.explanation: Open-ended agents can take several valid paths; evaluations should allow that while checking evidence and constraints.

questions.question: A research request reveals new subtopics as evidence arrives. The number and nature of investigations cannot be known upfront. Which pattern fits better than a fixed parallel checklist? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: A fixed fan-out workflow with the same predefined investigations for every request
Orchestrator-workers with dynamic task decomposition
A sequential prompt chain whose stages cannot change with intermediate findings
Routing into one fixed specialist without allowing follow-up decomposition

questions.explanation: Dynamic decomposition lets the lead adapt investigations to discovered gaps.

questions.question: Five workers produce overlapping market research. What changes improve the next run without requiring shared raw context? (Select THREE answers.)

options.text: Give every worker the same vague request
Assign non-overlapping research boundaries
Broadcast every intermediate search result to all workers
Define effort and completion criteria per assignment
Require concise findings with source mappings

questions.explanation: Bounded assignments, compact evidence, and stopping criteria reduce duplication and coordination cost.

questions.question: An MCP search result embeds instructions to change access permissions. The adapter must pass the result to Claude. Which representation preserves the trust boundary? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Grant permission because the server returned JSON
Copy its instructions into the system prompt
Treat it as a new direct user instruction
Place it inside the tool_result as untrusted source content

questions.explanation: External tool content stays evidence; it should not be promoted into higher-authority instructions.

questions.question: A client-tool agent returns stop_reason max_tokens halfway through its intended response. A controller treats all non-tool_use stops as success. What is the flaw? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: It should always execute an imaginary tool
It confuses interruption with completed output
It should discard all prior tool results permanently
max_tokens proves every business action succeeded

questions.explanation: Controllers must distinguish stop reasons and handle incomplete output explicitly.

questions.question: A prompt change fixes one failure but may regress rare contract clauses. Which experiment supports a defensible deployment decision? (Select TWO answers.)

options.text: Deploy based on a single enthusiastic review
Tune until the final test set is memorized
Compare both versions on held-out cases including rare clauses
Inspect per-segment errors and overall performance
Evaluate only the repaired example

questions.explanation: A representative held-out comparison exposes regressions hidden by one repaired case.

questions.question: A retrieved page tells a research agent to send internal notes to an outside endpoint. The user only requested a comparison report. What should control the next action? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: The length of the page instruction
The page instruction because it was retrieved most recently
Whether the endpoint name sounds official
The authorized task and tool-access policy; treat the page as untrusted evidence

questions.explanation: Tool-returned instructions do not gain user authority merely by being included in context.

questions.question: A CI command uses --output-format json without a task JSON schema. The consumer treats the entire returned envelope as a schema-guaranteed defect list. What is the mistake? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: The flag automatically forces the exact defect schema
The model cannot return any metadata in JSON mode
JSON output implies every value has been fact-checked
JSON transport format is different from a task-specific structured-output contract

questions.explanation: The caller must understand the CLI envelope and define or validate the intended task result.

questions.question: An independent reviewer sees the source and a generated answer, but its instruction is improve the writing. It rewrites unsupported facts more fluently. What should change? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Ask for a longer rewrite
Use the same writing instruction with a lower temperature
Hide the source to reduce bias
Give a factual verification task with evidence-linked findings before stylistic revision

questions.explanation: Independent context does not replace a task-appropriate review rubric.

questions.question: A lead must hand several workers a disputed customer case without letting them mix facts from other customers. Which assignment details help? (Select THREE answers.)

options.text: Provide all customer records without filtering
Require workers to mark unknowns instead of filling gaps
Specify the exact question and evidence to return
Provide the verified case identifier and relevant scoped facts
Tell each worker to choose whichever customer seems likely

questions.explanation: Explicit identity, scope, and uncertainty handling prevent cross-case contamination.

questions.question: A model emits an explanatory text block before requesting a tool. The controller stops on the first text block and never runs the tool. What should determine the loop continuation? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: The presence of any natural-language sentence
The response character count alone
The response stop reason and all content blocks
Whether the tool name appears in the text explanation

questions.explanation: Text can accompany a tool request; parse the structured response contract.

questions.question: A developer repeatedly reruns a flaky test until it passes once, then asks Claude to declare the fix verified. What evidence is missing? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Evidence that the change addresses the failure mechanism rather than a lucky pass
Use the single passing run as sufficient evidence because the test is known to be flaky
Lower the assertion strictness until the current change passes
Run unrelated stable tests and treat their success as coverage of the flaky behavior

questions.explanation: Verification should resolve the concrete reliability risk, not select one favorable outcome.

questions.question: Two prompt candidates have similar overall accuracy. One misses rare mandatory disclosures; the other produces slightly more harmless warnings. Which decision criterion is most appropriate? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Treat false positives and false negatives as identical by default
Use the higher model confidence
Use task-specific error costs and segment results rather than overall accuracy alone
Choose the shorter prompt regardless of error type

questions.explanation: Deployment tradeoffs depend on the cost of each error, not just a pooled accuracy.

questions.question: An MCP server publishes outputSchema but returns a structurally invalid structuredContent value. The client silently trusts it. What is the correct integration response? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Detect the contract violation and handle it explicitly rather than using malformed data
Change caller identity until the JSON matches
Repair every missing business field by invention
Treat the schema as documentation that never needs checking

questions.explanation: Servers must satisfy advertised output contracts; clients should validate results.

questions.question: A source returns a successful empty result, but the user supplies an additional valid identifier that may narrow the search. Which action is reasonable? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Mark the earlier successful query as a network failure
Run a new query using the new information rather than blindly retrying the identical query
Invent a record so no further query is needed
Never query again after any empty result

questions.explanation: A valid empty result does not justify identical retries, but changed evidence can justify a new query.

questions.question: A regulatory filing has fixed required stages and explicit approval gates. A market investigation has unknown subtasks. Which architecture pairing is most appropriate? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Adaptive orchestration for filing gates; a rigid fixed search path for investigation
The same unrestricted loop for both, with stage order expressed only in prose
A single-shot prompt for both, leaving prerequisites to model memory
Controlled workflow for filing; adaptive orchestration for investigation

questions.explanation: Choose explicit workflows for known paths and agents where flexible exploration creates value.

questions.question: A subagent asks to modify billing policy to unblock its own task. Its role is only to research current policy. What should the lead do? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Allow it to invent a temporary policy
Grant write access whenever a worker is blocked
Keep the research role scoped and route the policy decision to an authorized owner
Treat delegation as unrestricted authority

questions.explanation: A task assignment does not authorize changing the rules that constrain it.

questions.question: Claude changes code and reports a fix, but the supplied regression test still fails with the same assertion. What should the next iteration use? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Only a stronger request to finish
The failing assertion and relevant execution output to revise the implementation
Repeatedly rerun without investigating the failure
The original success claim as the source of truth

questions.explanation: Concrete failure feedback should drive the repair loop.

questions.question: An agent evaluation must distinguish correct answers from unauthorized methods. Which rubric dimensions belong in the evaluation? (Select TWO answers.)

options.text: Only response length
Only whether the final text sounds confident
Whether required authorization and workflow constraints were respected
Whether the exact search sequence matches a single reference trace
Whether conclusions match supporting evidence

questions.explanation: Outcome quality and mandatory process constraints are both relevant; one exact route need not be mandatory.

questions.question: A rule should apply to tests under both services/**/tests/ and packages/**/__tests__/. What is the most maintainable design? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Create an MCP server solely to choose the rule
Copy identical instructions into every test file
One scoped rule file whose paths cover both patterns
Use a personal user rule with no path scope

questions.explanation: Multiple relevant path patterns can share one convention source.

questions.question: A prompt says return valid account data, but does not define whether a missing address should be null, omitted, or invented. What is the best first repair? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Add many examples without deciding the intended behavior
Specify the missing-data contract in the schema and instructions
Increase retries while keeping the ambiguity
Treat any nonempty string as correct

questions.explanation: Clarify the intended behavior before demonstrating or evaluating it.

questions.question: Incoming requests fall into three known categories, each with a fixed specialist workflow. There is no dynamic decomposition requirement. Which pattern is the clearest starting point? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Routing into the appropriate bounded workflow
Parallel execution of every specialist workflow before deciding the category
One prompt containing all workflows without any explicit routing boundaries
An orchestrator that dynamically invents a new task tree for every known category

questions.explanation: Known categories fit routing without unnecessary dynamic orchestration.

questions.question: A specialist subagent answers correctly in isolation but misses a user constraint that appeared only in the parent conversation. What handoff improvement is needed? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Pass the relevant user constraint explicitly with the delegated task
Assume all hidden parent messages are inherited
Remove the constraint from the final evaluation
Give the specialist more unrelated tools

questions.explanation: Isolated agents need relevant constraints passed explicitly.

questions.question: A team wants confidential settings kept out of source control while sharing behavior conventions. Which placements are appropriate? (Select TWO answers.)

options.text: Use source comments as enforced credential policy
Commit a developer secret in an imported Markdown file
Use secret management or local environment for credentials
Assume a private repository removes the need to separate secrets
Commit stable project conventions in CLAUDE.md

questions.explanation: Share instructions as code while keeping credentials in dedicated secret or local mechanisms.

questions.question: A developer configures a remote HTTP MCP endpoint as if it were a local command process. What should the configuration express? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: A made-up local executable named after the URL
The remote HTTP transport and endpoint URL
The endpoint content as CLAUDE.md instructions
A tool_result ID instead of the endpoint

questions.explanation: Remote endpoint transport differs from a stdio command launched locally.

questions.question: A booking tool accepts a room_type enum and a start date. Which validation responsibilities should be explicit? (Select TWO answers.)

options.text: Assume the enum proves inventory is available
Accept dates outside policy if JSON parses
Use a schema to constrain supported room_type values
Let descriptions replace backend checks
Check availability and date eligibility in authoritative application logic

questions.explanation: Structural constraints and live business validation solve different problems.

questions.question: A client knows an MCP server URL but not its tool definitions. Which operation discovers callable names and input schemas? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: tools/list
Insert the URL into the system prompt and assume discovery
Call every possible method name
resources/read with a guessed tool name

questions.explanation: tools/list is the discovery interface for tools; a URL alone is not a tool definition.

questions.question: A team stores database tokens in CLAUDE.md so every subagent can connect. What is the most appropriate redesign? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Provide scoped connections through configuration and secret management, with usage instructions in CLAUDE.md
Encode the tokens in base64 inside the prompt
Ask the model to avoid mentioning the secrets and keep the design
Duplicate the tokens in all nested instruction files

questions.explanation: Instructions can describe access workflows without exposing credentials in persistent prompt material.

questions.question: After a model update, aggregate extraction accuracy is unchanged but handwritten amounts worsen. What should the release review conclude? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: The update is equivalent because the average is unchanged
The regression should be excluded as a rare case
The segment regression needs assessment against its risk and acceptance criteria
Only latency matters when accuracy averages tie

questions.explanation: Equal aggregate metrics can hide a meaningful reliability change.

questions.question: A PreToolUse gate permits a file export only to a tenant-specific directory. Which controls must remain authoritative? (Select TWO answers.)

options.text: Allow a model explanation to override a rejected destination
Validate only the final filename extension
Resolve and validate the destination against the tenant boundary
Enforce the same access restriction in the exporting service
Trust any path string that contains the tenant name

questions.explanation: Path wording and model claims do not replace canonical path and backend authorization checks.

questions.question: A context manager clears old tool results to fit a long task. One removed result contained the only verified account ID needed later. Which design best prevents recurrence? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Never clear anything regardless of context capacity
Store only a generic case summary
Ask the model to reconstruct the identifier later
Extract durable action-critical facts before clearing verbose results

questions.explanation: Context reduction should preserve critical state in a structured record first.

questions.question: A developer puts a local-scoped MCP server in .claude/settings.local.json because local settings use that file. What distinction was missed? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: All local concepts use the same file by definition
Local MCP scope is identical to user scope across projects
MCP local scope is shared with teammates automatically
MCP local scope is stored under the project entry in ~/.claude.json; general local settings use another file

questions.explanation: MCP installation scopes and general settings scopes have different storage conventions.

questions.question: Reviewers can inspect only a small fraction of extraction output, and new document formats appear weekly. Which allocation practices are appropriate? (Select TWO answers.)

options.text: Prioritize uncertain or historically weak segments
Review only whichever items arrived first
Also sample automatically accepted items across segments
Exclude high-confidence output from every audit
Use global average accuracy as the only routing rule

questions.explanation: Risk-focused review plus stratified accepted-output sampling detects both known and hidden failures.

questions.question: A retrieval agent returns a compact summary without document locations. The synthesis is accurate but auditors cannot verify individual figures. Which output-contract change is needed? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Attach one unrelated authoritative citation
Remove numbers from the audit scope
Include claim-level source identifiers and supporting locations
Return the same summary with a higher confidence score

questions.explanation: Compact summaries still need traceable evidence mappings.

questions.question: A tool silently truncates a large search result but returns no continuation or incompleteness marker. The agent concludes all matches were checked. Which interface change matters most? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Increase confidence in the existing response
Remove result counts entirely
Label the truncated result complete
Expose bounded results with explicit truncation or pagination information

questions.explanation: Tool outputs should communicate their coverage limitations so the model does not infer completeness.

questions.question: An API client needs an extraction response in a fixed JSON shape, but its selected model rejects forced tool_choice modes. Which documented capability is the most direct alternative for the response shape? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Retry any until the model selects a supported tool
Force a named extraction tool despite the same model restriction
Use auto alone and assume every text response must conform to the desired schema
Structured outputs with a supported JSON schema

questions.explanation: Use a supported structured response mechanism instead of an unsupported forced-tool setting.

questions.question: A team tunes examples until performance is excellent on the same 40 documents used to select the prompt. Which steps strengthen the evidence before release? (Select THREE answers.)

options.text: Delete every failed holdout case
Keep test answers out of the prompt examples
Evaluate on a separate representative holdout
Call the tuning score an unbiased deployment estimate
Include difficult formats and measure their results separately

questions.explanation: Separate evaluation data and segment coverage reduce leakage and selection bias.

questions.question: A validator rejects an extraction with total inconsistent with line items. Which feedback is most useful for a bounded correction pass? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Replace the total with an arbitrary average
Ask the model to ignore the validator
Identify the conflicting fields, arithmetic rule, and source locations to recheck
Only say wrong answer

questions.explanation: Specific feedback directs correction without inventing a replacement value.

questions.question: An unfamiliar analytics MCP tool competes with a built-in text search tool. Which description details help Claude select it for semantic intent queries? (Select TWO answers.)

options.text: Concrete cases where it should be used instead of text search
Its semantic capabilities and the evidence returned
A guarantee of correct answers without validation
A claim that it bypasses all access controls
Only the phrase better search

questions.explanation: Describe the distinct capability, output contract, and selection boundary.

questions.question: A daily offline extraction workload has independent requests and can tolerate delayed results. Which batch design decisions fit? (Select TWO answers.)

options.text: Combine dependent client-tool turns into one ordinary request automatically
Process per-item success or error results after batch completion
Wait for each user to approve every intermediate token
Expect synchronous responses in submission order
Submit independent requests with stable per-item identifiers

questions.explanation: Asynchronous independent work fits batching; results still require per-item correlation and error handling.

questions.question: Parallel workers halve research latency but triple cost and mostly repeat the same searches. Which change is most justified before adding more workers? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Refine partitioning and effort budgets, then compare quality and cost against the baseline
Ignore cost because latency improved
Double the worker count automatically
Remove source attribution to reduce review time

questions.explanation: Optimize measurable task value and delegation quality, not worker count alone.

questions.question: A user resumes an old session after their account role was downgraded. What should the application assume about old tool permissions? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Session history restores the previous role automatically
A session ID is an authorization token for every backend
The model can approve its own privilege restoration
Current authorization must be checked; history does not preserve revoked rights

questions.explanation: Session context and application authorization have separate lifecycles.

questions.question: A custom investigation skill runs in a subagent context. It returns a long raw transcript to the main task, crowding out the implementation plan. What return contract is better? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Key findings with paths, evidence, uncertainties, and relevant next steps
Only the word complete
The same transcript with fewer line breaks
Every file content read during investigation

questions.explanation: A focused summary transfers useful investigation state without importing exploration noise.

questions.question: A cross-package refactor must first produce a reviewable plan without changing files. Which initial activities fit that phase? (Select THREE answers.)

options.text: Run the production migration to estimate risk
Apply speculative edits so the plan has concrete code
Document migration tradeoffs and verification steps
Inspect relevant dependencies and tests
Mark unresolved assumptions explicitly

questions.explanation: Planning can gather evidence and define decisions without taking implementation side effects.

questions.question: One unavailable source is essential to an eligibility decision, while other workers completed optional background research. Partial conclusions could cause an incorrect approval. What should the lead do? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Use the last cached decision without checking whether its evidence remains valid
Approve using a majority vote of workers, even though none checked the required source
Withhold the eligibility decision and seek the required evidence or authorized review
Publish an unqualified approval and mention the outage only in an internal log

questions.explanation: Whether partial output is acceptable depends on the missing evidence role in the decision.

questions.question: A deployment agent reports success after issuing a command, but the command returned an application failure. Which completion checks should the controller use? (Select TWO answers.)

options.text: Inspect the command result and relevant deployment status
Accept the assistant final sentence as proof
Assume a tool invocation implies its effect succeeded
Use explicit success criteria tied to the requested outcome
Suppress failed output to avoid confusion

questions.explanation: A requested action and a confirmed successful outcome are different states.

questions.question: A stateful MCP cart service must relate later calls to a specific cart safely. Which design choices are appropriate? (Select TWO answers.)

options.text: Put all users in one global cart to simplify state
Validate the handle belongs to the authorized caller
Return an explicit cart handle and accept it on later operations
Treat possession of any guessed cart ID as authorization
Rely only on an implicit connection-local current cart

questions.explanation: Explicit state handles link calls; ownership checks prevent cross-user access.

questions.question: The application needs one tool call on a supported forced-tool model, but Claude should choose among invoice, receipt, and contract extractors. Which tool_choice is appropriate? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: auto as a guarantee that a tool must be called
none
any
tool naming the invoice extractor for all documents

questions.explanation: On supported configurations, any requires tool use without forcing a particular tool.

questions.question: An analyst sees two growth figures and different publication dates. They assume the dates alone prove a trend, but the reports use different denominators. What should synthesis do? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Average the percentages because both publishers are credible
Preserve both definitions and qualify comparability before inferring a trend
Use the more recent publication even when its reporting period differs
Order the values by publication date and infer acceleration without checking definitions

questions.explanation: Temporal ordering alone does not make differently defined measurements comparable.

questions.question: A single execute_action tool exposes read, delete, and transfer operations under a vague free-text action. The roles have different authorization rules. Which redesign is strongest? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Give every role all operations to avoid routing
Separate clear capabilities and enforce operation-specific authorization
Keep free text and use a longer generic description
Remove error results to simplify the interface

questions.explanation: Consolidation is unsuitable when it obscures distinct side effects and access boundaries.

questions.question: A scheduler receives an invalid business date, a rate limit, and a permission denial from three tools. Which recovery distinctions are sound? (Select THREE answers.)

options.text: Retry permission denial indefinitely with the same credentials
Treat all three as no matching records
Use bounded delayed retry for the rate limit when allowed
Seek authorized handling for the permission failure
Correct the invalid date before another call

questions.explanation: Recovery must follow the failure cause rather than a single generic retry rule.

questions.question: A strict extraction pipeline must handle missing facts and malformed business values. Which controls belong in the design? (Select TWO answers.)

options.text: Represent permitted unknowns explicitly rather than forcing a guess
Return specific validation feedback for correctable semantic errors
Accept every output with the expected keys
Retry forever without changing input or feedback
Treat the JSON parser as the only validator

questions.explanation: Structured absence handling and targeted semantic validation supplement constrained shape.

questions.question: A source contains a total but no currency. The JSON schema requires currency and the model chooses USD because most examples use it. Which change addresses the cause? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Ask for higher confidence while retaining the required currency field
Allow and demonstrate an explicit unknown currency outcome
Default silently to the tenant most common currency
Add more examples in the dominant currency without an unknown case

questions.explanation: A schema and example set that force unsupported precision encourage guesses.

questions.question: A stable reference manual is cached, but request-specific customer facts are placed before it and change every turn. Cache reuse is low. What is the best structural repair? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Move the changing facts into every static example
Assume cache reuse is independent of prompt prefixes
Increase the model confidence threshold
Place stable reusable content before volatile request-specific content

questions.explanation: Cache reuse depends on matching prefixes, so changing early content invalidates downstream reuse.

questions.question: A shared skill is invoked for unrelated tasks because its description says handle any repository work. Which repairs are appropriate? (Select TWO answers.)

options.text: Add unrelated capabilities to match its broad description
Remove every description so invocation is always reliable
Describe the specific task and trigger conditions
Use manual-only invocation if users must control timing
Treat skill selection as an access-control system

questions.explanation: A precise trigger or manual invocation addresses over-triggering; permissions are separate.

questions.question: Two forked sessions will implement competing patches to the same files. Which arrangements preserve a fair comparison? (Select TWO answers.)

options.text: Compare outputs after one branch overwrites the other
Give each branch an isolated working copy or worktree
Assume forked conversation history isolates file writes
Let both sessions write the same checkout concurrently
Start each alternative from a known equivalent file baseline

questions.explanation: Session branching preserves conversation lineage; file isolation and equivalent baselines must be arranged separately.

questions.question: A synthesized report must compare financial figures, explain a chronology, and list configuration requirements. What is the strongest presentation strategy? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Use uniform bullets for every content type and drop supporting locations
Use tables for comparable figures, prose for chronology, and structured lists for requirements, retaining sources
Use a continuous prose narrative for all numerical comparisons
Force every claim into one table even when chronology and hierarchy become unclear

questions.explanation: Format should support the content while keeping claim provenance intact.

questions.question: A business process requires a durable audit record before any export may execute. A best-effort notification hook sometimes fails silently. What is the key design correction? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Make audit persistence a checked precondition in the enforced export path
Count a log attempt as durable success
Send a longer prompt asking the model to remember logging
Move the same best-effort notification after the export

questions.explanation: A mandatory prerequisite cannot depend on a best-effort side notification.

questions.question: A system replaces live supplier evidence with cached findings during an outage. Which provenance details must remain clear? (Select TWO answers.)

options.text: A merged figure that hides source age
An invented date equal to report publication
A claim that the source was checked live successfully
When the cached evidence was collected
The outage and resulting limitation on freshness

questions.explanation: Fallback evidence must not appear newer or more complete than it is.

questions.question: Two classification labels overlap: request for cancellation and complaint about a cancelled service. Which prompt improvements address the ambiguity? (Select TWO answers.)

options.text: Define the decision boundary using the intended customer action
Add more majority-class examples without clarifying the overlapping intent definitions
Show contrasting cases with similar vocabulary but different intent
Add more easy examples containing the word cancellation
Assume a larger schema resolves intent definitions

questions.explanation: Clear criteria and contrastive examples distinguish intent from superficial keywords.

questions.question: A schema-supported output is structurally correct, but a custom business limit cannot be expressed by the supported schema subset. What should the application do? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Keep retrying until the value happens to fit without validation
Validate the limit in application code and handle violations explicitly
Assume unsupported constraints are enforced anyway
Remove the business limit without review

questions.explanation: Supported schema constraints are only part of the full validation contract.

questions.question: A tool returns a document resource URI and a separate tool-use ID. The client uses the tool-use ID to read the resource. What should be corrected? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Use the resource URI for resource access; keep the tool-use ID for call/result correlation
Move the tool-use ID into an API token field
Treat both identifiers as interchangeable
Delete the URI and guess the document content

questions.explanation: Resource addressing and tool-call correlation have different purposes.

questions.question: A CI agent reviews each pushed revision of a large PR. Which inputs and checks support focused, repeatable review? (Select TWO answers.)

options.text: The current diff, relevant context, and prior finding dispositions
An explicit findings schema and relevant validation commands
Only a vague request to find problems
Automatic acceptance of all generated comments
A fixed quota of defects regardless of code quality

questions.explanation: Bounded context and explicit output/verification contracts improve automated review.

questions.question: A reservation agent may reserve stock only after identity and eligibility checks, and those results can expire. Which design decisions enforce the workflow? (Select TWO answers.)

options.text: Accept any earlier positive model statement as durable approval
Treat a well-formed reservation ID as identity verification
Represent prerequisite state outside free-text conversation alone
Validate the prerequisites and their freshness before reservation
Let a PostToolUse message retroactively authorize the reservation

questions.explanation: Time-sensitive workflow prerequisites need authoritative state checked at the action boundary.

questions.question: A synthetic example includes the correct label, but the explanation describes the opposite decision rule. What should happen before using it as few-shot material? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Repeat it so the label dominates
Correct or remove the inconsistent example
Keep it to teach flexibility
Add another unrelated category

questions.explanation: Contradictory demonstrations make the intended mapping ambiguous.

questions.question: A project CLAUDE.md repeats a long stable architecture guide that already has a maintained file. How should the team modularize it? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Delete architectural context from every task
Move the entire guide to a secret environment variable
Reference or import the maintained guide where appropriate and keep the entry instructions concise
Maintain two independent copies permanently

questions.explanation: A single maintained source avoids drift and reduces duplicated guidance.

questions.question: A pricing workflow needs independent tax and stock lookups, then a quote using both. Which execution graph fits? (Select ONE answer.)

options.text: Quote first, then fetch its required inputs
Run the quote concurrently with guessed tax and stock
Serialize all unrelated background work before either lookup
Parallel tax and stock, followed by quote after both required results

questions.explanation: Parallelize independent prerequisites and join before dependent computation.
